conventions.commits: Conventional commits (type(scope): subject, e.g. feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)); GPG signed and DCO Signed-off-by per issue acceptance criteria; .commitlintrc.yml present at repo root.

conventions.linting: cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --check; workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt via cfg_attr); cargo deny check advisories licenses; REUSE compliance.
conventions.error_handling: Query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError with the language name; handlers return Option or empty Vec and use bounds-checked get_node_text or slice-by-byte-range; tests use expect with messages.

patterns: Registry triad: a languages/<lang>.rs module with query consts, a LanguageInfo arm in get_language_info, and a get_ts_language arm; plus EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages in lang.rs (java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs all follow it).
Java DEFUSE_QUERY uses per-capture prefixes write.local, write.assign, writeread.update and read.usage; parser_elements.rs classifies by prefix and dedupes reads at write offsets.
Java extract_inheritance walks named fields (superclass, interfaces) and prefixes results with 'extends ' and 'implements '; Swift walks named children and uses 'extends'/'conforms'.

Element captures: 'function' captures the whole declaration, 'func_name' or 'method_name' the name; 'class' captures the whole type declaration, 'class_name' or 'type_name' the name; parser_elements falls back to child_by_field_name('name').
Import query captures the whole declaration (import_declaration in Java, import_declaration in Swift); CSS captures the string value inside import_statement.
Grammar crates are consumed as tree_sitter_<lang>::LANGUAGE.into() (LANGUAGE_TYPESCRIPT and LANGUAGE_TSX for TypeScript); tree-sitter-php exposes LANGUAGE_PHP and LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY instead.
Query compilation is lazy per language (#1786), so a malformed query fails on first use; a unit test that compiles every query is the guard.

The crate's lib.rs doc example asserts !tree.root_node().has_error() on a mixed <?php file, which supports the acceptance criterion.

library_findings.relevant_api: Query::new(&Language, &str) -> Result<Query, QueryError>; Query::capture_names(); Node::child_by_field_name; Node::named_child; Node::kind; Node::parent
library_findings.notes: Context7 (/websites/rs_tree-sitter) confirmed the signatures above. child_by_field_name returns None for base_clause and class_interface_clause because they have no field name, so the walk must iterate named children and match kinds.

approaches.name: A: Java-mirror registry wiring with kind-based inheritance walk (recommended)
approaches.description: New languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY ((named_type (name))), IMPORT_QUERY ((namespace_use_declaration)), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name based), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause by node kind. Uses tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP. extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type stay None per the issue.
pros: Matches the Java and Swift registry shape the issue names as templates
Keeps LANGUAGE_PHP so HTML-mixed templates parse without ERROR nodes, satisfying the acceptance criterion
No new handler plumbing; out-of-scope handlers stay None
Grammar fields verified in php/src/node-types.json, so queries can be unit-tested before wiring
cons: Inheritance walk must be kind-based because base_clause and class_interface_clause have no field names
Interface extends and class extends both map to base_clause, so the walk must branch on the parent kind to label interfaces correctly if desired
Cargo.lock entry needs the 7-day package age check to be confirmed on crates.io, which this scout could not reach

approaches.name: B: Java-parity with the three optional handlers added
approaches.description: Approach A plus extract_function_name (function_definition and method_declaration name field), find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type (walk up to class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration or enum_declaration), mirroring java.rs lines 41-127.
pros: Receiver lookup would be ready if a future consumer appears
cons: Explicitly out of scope in the issue (no consumer since #1807)
Adds roughly 100 lines of untested-by-consumer surface and more unit tests
Violates the issue's scope rule against implementing features not specified

approaches.name: C: Use LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for .php files
approaches.description: Register tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY (the php_only grammar) instead of LANGUAGE_PHP, so pure PHP files get a grammar without the HTML text node.
pros: Smaller tree for pure PHP files
Avoids the text node path entirely
cons: Fails the acceptance criterion that a mixed HTML and <?php file parses with zero ERROR nodes
Would need a second grammar switch by content, which the registry does not support
Adds a dialect decision the issue did not ask for

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that keeps the issue's scope, uses LANGUAGE_PHP so HTML-mixed files parse cleanly, and follows the Java/Swift registry shape. The inheritance walk must be kind-based because the grammar gives base_clause and class_interface_clause no field names; Approach B adds handlers the issue excludes and Approach C fails the mixed-template acceptance criterion.

(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class

inheritance_walk_citation: Start at the class_declaration node (kind 'class_declaration'; fields: attributes, body, name only; no parent_class/base_classes/interfaces field exists). Field-based access is not available for inheritance. Step 1: iterate named children of class_declaration; for each child whose kind is 'base_clause' (the 'extends' clause), iterate its named children, which are of kind 'name', 'qualified_name' or 'relative_name' (the hidden _name rule expands inline, so these have no field name), and push format!("extends {text}") using source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()]. Step 2: for each child whose kind is 'class_interface_clause' (the 'implements' clause), iterate its named children of the same three kinds and push format!("implements {text}") per name. Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter-php common/define-grammar.js, class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list))); base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)); class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). php/src/node-types.json lists class_declaration children types base_clause and class_interface_clause with multiple=true, and base_clause/class_interface_clause children types name, qualified_name, relative_name. Interface: interface_declaration uses optional($.base_clause) (so 'interface I extends A, B' yields extends A and extends B). Enum: enum_declaration uses optional($.class_interface_clause) only. Trait: trait_declaration has no clause nodes, so the walk returns []. Class with no clauses: no base_clause or class_interface_clause child, returns [].
